newsitem.title: GERMANY: German cocoa buyers continue to hold back.
newsitem.headline: German cocoa buyers continue to hold back.

text.p: German cocoa traders said buying was hesitant as sterling-denominated futures were range-bound and the British currency remained strong versus the mark, albeit off earlier highs.
"There is enough cocoa around so there is no urgency, although consumers are interested in buying dips," one said.
"But they're relaxed because they believe futures rallies would be stopped by origin selling."
The industry was also awaiting firmer Ivorian arrivals data, including mid-crop forecasts, before taking long-term decisions, traders said.
February/March cif Ivorian bean sellers were unchanged from last week at 2.28 marks per kg.
The first quarter cocoa butter ratio was up two points at 2.66 and the implied mark price liquid ex-works was 6.14 marks (6.09), basis March.
Basis May and based on a ratio of 2.60, butter would cost 6.17 marks.
Sterling was at 2.7316 marks at the Frankfurt exchange fixing at midday (2.7467 last week).
